To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
location and output are independent when the production function exhibits linear homogeneity, transport rates do not vary with output, and location is constrained to the Moses arc.
location is independent (dependent) of output if the production function is (is not) homogeneous of degree one and if the transport rate function has constant elasticities (does not).
location is independent if the production function is linearly homogeneous, and the transport rate function has a constant elasticity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not the location of a firm is independent of output and the results indicate that the answer depends on the functional forms of the production and transport rate functions.
the question of the effect of output on location when transport rates depend on the amount shipped.
the following question: What is the role of location in a general equilibrium model of production and trade when transport rates depend on output quantities?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Moses-type model is not sufficiently general to provide an adequate framework for the theory of production and location.

if one is willing to accept the assumption that transport rates depend on the quantities shipped, then one can have a model in which the location of production depends on the level of output and in which the level of output depends on the location of production.

if transport rates do depend on quantities shipped and if the production function is linearly homogeneous, then the theory of production and location must be developed in the framework of an input- output model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the theory of production is not sufficient to determine location when transport rates are a function of quantities shipped, and that the theory of location is not sufficient to describe the theory of production.

if transport rate functions have elasticities of transport rate which are independent of quantities shipped, then a production function linearly homogeneous is sufficient to insure that output and location are independent.
if the transport rate function is not linearly homogeneous, then the location is a function of the level of output.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transport rate functions are important determinants of the relationship between output and location.
, in the context of the generalized Moses framework, the location and production decisions are interdependent and the location decision is not independent of the production decision.
if the production function is linearly homogeneous and the transport rate is independent of output, then the location is independent of production.
